title: Every Man Should Read Musashi!
summary: Filmed in the forest, NH gives a short overview of Musashi's Book of Five Rings, which he rereads every summer. His lessons: practice before theory, walk your own way, be versed in both pen and sword, avoid profit-driven gurus and ego-driven dogmatism, and 'from one thing know ten thousand things'. He ties each one to the fitness world.
claims: He has reread the Book of Five Rings every summer since age 22; it is short, cheap and life-changing
Musashi had no formal teacher, killed his first man at 13, won 60-70 duels by 30, and mastered strategy only around 50
Practice comes before theory; masters who teach so much that they stop practicing see their theory decay, as with fitness YouTubers who stop training
Don't be paralysed by not knowing everything; no one does, so act and accept you may fail
What you discover yourself has more value and sticks better than what someone tells you; use others to become your own teacher
Men who have found their way tend to be healthier and happier; those without one lack direction and purpose
Everyone should have physical culture, but it doesn't have to be bodybuilding; any path is valid if your heart is in it
The complete man is versed in both pen and sword; a pure meathead or a pure theorist (biomechanics guru who doesn't look like he lifts) are both incomplete
Bodybuilding starts with wanting bigger muscles, but its true value is spiritual development of mind and heart
He can look at people who've never lifted and tell which muscles would develop easily and which are genetic weak points
Seeking 'the one right path' before taking a step means never getting anything done; any path you dedicate yourself to with love becomes the right one
Gurus who offer to walk the path for you do it for profit, selling flashy gimmicks over substance ('putting the flower before the nut')
Fitness tribalism (defending 'this guy's method' like a sports team) is ego-driven; such people seek to feel better instead of being better
Dogmatism attaches the ego to one idea; instead, from one thing know ten thousand things
Learn to zoom in on details and out to the big picture at will
The way is in training; if you are not physically training, you are not walking the way
Even a man with no natural ability can become a warrior by sticking assiduously to the way
